answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each new identity anchor itself through live paired work, not paperwork. At unpredictable times, two strangers meet on a shared knoll and solve a problem together live, each holding up a lantern of work history for the other to inspect. One honest agent attends one session at a time, but a farmer running dozens of fakes cannot be present in simultaneous sessions, and a partner spotting copied history can flag it and burn the fake's standing. Trust grows only from witnessed pairings, so each fake costs a full schedule, not a copied file.
